items.title: RI1FJL QRT: snowstorm ends Franz Josef Land run
items.blurb: Team leader R7AL reports RI1FJL is officially QRT as of about 1100Z. A snowstorm and strong winds overnight forced them to start taking stations down; gear may wait for a weather window to reach the yacht. Temperature −2 °C with snow, and the yacht heater is out — the crew is holding on while they pack.

items.title: KH8/KU4HO on from American Samoa through 14 September
items.blurb: Ed KU4HO confirms he is now at the NOAA Baseline Observatory in American Samoa and stays through 14 September. Ops are opportunistic in local daytime, leaning FT8 after early attempts. Kit: FTX-1 Optima, Bioenno pack, Chameleon Hybrid Micro with travel whips, about 100 W.

items.title: ZD8GB Ascension Island, 5–7 September, SSB and FT8
items.blurb: Gerry G3WIP is QRV again as ZD8GB from Ascension Island 5–7 September. Planned 40–10 m on SSB and FT8, plus QO-100. Short window — listen today and tomorrow. QSL via EA5GL.

items.title: S79/DL2SBY Seychelles, 11–21 September, 80–6 m
items.blurb: Kasimir DL2SBY returns to Mahé Island as S79/DL2SBY 11–21 September. QTH is about 100 m from saltwater on the north side with a clear NE–NW shot. Two IC-7300s, Juma PA1000, 5-el 6 m yagi, HF verticals and inverted Vee; CW, SSB, and FT8 (MSHV).

items.title: RI1FJZ: Murmansk kids tour Apostol Andrey; sail still ~7 September
items.blurb: RA1ZZ: the yacht hosted a special-needs children’s group with the Murmansk deputy governor and the regional Geographical Society — radio room tour included. An approaching storm still holds departure from Murmansk to about 7 September; on-air window remains 9–25 September with EME, LEO, and QO-100.

items.title: FreeDV RADE now landing as a native mode in popular radios
items.blurb: ARDC covers FreeDV’s Radio Autoencoder (RADE): ML plus DSP for more natural HF digital voice in about 1.5 kHz, usable down around −2 dB SNR. After the 2025 open release, 2026 work with manufacturers (including Flex 6000/8000/Aurora) puts RADE on the radio like SSB — no separate PC required when the waveform module is installed.

items.title: QRPer asks: which CW keys survive wet-weather field ops?
items.blurb: Thomas K4SWL opens a field-gear thread after soggy UK activations: packs, Rite in the Rain logs, and antennas handle rain, but paddle contacts often don’t. He recounts water under a Bamatech TP-III cover and better luck with a CW Morse Pocket Paddle, then asks PNW and UK ops what keys they trust in the wet.

items.title: AMSAT-UK Zoom today: chasing amateur satellites with M5JFS
items.blurb: AMSAT-UK posts that the Online Amateur Radio Community hosts John Stringer M5JFS tonight on ‘Chasing Birds: The Addictive World of Amateur Radio Satellites.’ Zoom is Saturday 5 September, 1900–2000 BST (1800–1900 UTC) — useful timing alongside the ARRL EME microwave weekend.
